title: P0 hosted API rate-spiral throttle handoff postmortem
summary: On 2026-12-07 at ~09:17 UTC the Hosted API experienced a rapid escalation of p98/p99 latency and a spike in 5xx errors affecting streaming and non-streaming endpoints. The trigger was a feedback loop between a recently deployed fair-queueing patch on the edge proxy and client adaptive backoff heuristics which caused a rate-spiral: clients increased concurrency as latency temporarily dropped, then were sharply throttled by the new queueing policy, which led to simultaneous reconnects and amplified KV cache pressure. The resulting conditions saturated acceptor queues and evicted streaming sessions, producing widespread short-duration 5xx waves and fragmented streaming responses.
impact: ~12% of requests during the 44-minute window returned 5xx or streaming fragments. Several high-throughput customers saw degraded tail latency and transient error rates over 100x their baseline. Background jobs queued on Dedicated fallback paths experienced increased retries. No data loss or customer data exposure occurred. Estimated customer-visible downtime window: 00:09:17–00:09:59 UTC (primary spike) with smaller recurrence waves until mitigation fully applied at 10:01 UTC.
detection_and_alerting: On-call pager fired for p98 latency and error-rate SLO alerts. Automated runbook suggested scaling edge pool and toggling new fair-queueing flag. Early alerts were noisy due to metric cardinality; initial paging routed to edge SRE instead of serving-runtime because the alert source tag was edge-proxy.
timeline: 09:05 UTC - CI rollout of fair-queueing v2 to edge-proxy (canary -> 30% -> 100% roll) begins
09:16 UTC - First p99 latency jump detected in US-W region (edge-proxy telemetry)
09:17 UTC - Global SLO alert: p98 latency > SLO and 5xx rate > 5x baseline; on-call paged
09:20 UTC - Observed client-side adaptive backoff patterns (bulk reconnects) in traces; KV cache pressure rises
09:25 UTC - Initial mitigation attempted: increase edge acceptor threads and widen queue depth (temporary) — no durable effect
09:33 UTC - Rollback of fair-queueing v2 to v1 on edge-proxy started
09:40 UTC - Temporary global request cap (soft throttle) applied at gateway to damp reconnect storms
09:48 UTC - KV cache eviction rate normalizing; streaming reconnections drop sharply
10:01 UTC - Error rates fall back to baseline; post-incident monitoring/validation continues
10:30 UTC - Hotfix submitted: add jitter to adaptive client backoff guidance and instrument queue-length telemetry in more granular buckets
root_cause: A combination of: (1) fair-queueing v2 changed head-of-line scheduling semantics that temporarily reduced latency for short flows but increased tail variance for heavy-prefixed sessions; (2) many SDK clients use an aggressive adaptive concurrency heuristic that increases concurrent streams when latency appears low — those clients ramped up concurrency during the initial canary windows; (3) the resulting burst of concurrent requests triggered stricter server-side throttles and queue compaction which caused mass reconnects and KV-cache churn; and (4) alert routing and insufficient guardrails around the rollout allowed the change to reach full rollout before we observed the emergent feedback loop in production.
mitigation: Immediate rollback of fair-queueing v2 to v1 on all edge-proxy nodes
Applied a global soft request-cap at gateway to limit reconnection fanout
Increased acceptor and worker thread pools as a short-term headroom measure
Opened priority-only lanes for long-lived streaming sessions to avoid eviction during storms
remediation: Rework fair-queueing v2: add per-tenant smoothing and avoid aggressive compaction when prefix-hotspots detected
Add rollout gating: require 6-hour canary observation windows and synthetic burst tests before >30% rollout
Instrument queue-length, per-tenant concurrency, and client-backoff signals with high-cardinality retention for 72 hours
Update SDK guidance: add recommended jitter and max-concurrency defaults to prevent optimistic bursts
Build an automated canary guard that simulates client adaptive heuristics under the new scheduling policy
follow_up_actions: Postmortem review with Edge, Serving-Runtime, and SDK teams scheduled 2026-12-11
Create a chaos test that reproduces adaptive-client + queueing interactions and add to presubmit for edge-proxy PRs
Add an alert that triggers when client reconnects exceed X per minute for any single tenant
Ship SDK patch to default-enable jitter and reduce max concurrency from 16 to 8 in long-polling paths
Run a customer-impact sweep and notify top affected customers with remediation summary and support credits where appropriate
lessons_learned: Systemic interactions across components (client heuristics + server scheduling) can create non-linear failure modes not visible in single-service tests
Short rollout windows without simulated adversarial loads allow fragile behavior to reach production quickly
Metric cardinality and alert routing matter — ensure alerts carry both component and tenant tags to route correctly
Runbooks must include a fast rollback path for scheduling/policy changes and a default global dampening control
runbook_changes: Add a new section for 'scheduling-policy regressions' with steps: disable policy flag -> apply global soft-cap -> divert streaming to priority lanes
Document forced-canary procedure: preserve 30% capacity and inject synthetic burst traffic for 2 hours before wider rollout
Add checklist item for release: verify SDK concurrency guidance is published alongside server-side policy changes
metrics_snapshot: p98 latency peaked at 1.8s (baseline 120ms), 5xx rate peaked at 12% (baseline 0.1%), streaming session disconnects spiked to 6k/min (baseline 30/min). CPU and memory on edge-proxies remained <70% but acceptor queue length and RPC latencies spiked markedly.
reproduction_steps: Locally reproduce with integrated test harness: run 500 synthetic clients that implement adaptive concurrency (increase concurrency when observed RTT < 150ms), deploy fair-queueing v2 to test edge, and run for 30 minutes; measure queue compaction, reconnect frequency, and KV-cache eviction. Load-test harness PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/chaos/issue/552
notes_to_oncall: If similar symptoms reappear (p98 latency + reconnect spikes): 1) apply global soft-cap immediately, 2) start rollback of recent scheduling flags, 3) open communication to SDK-team to temporarily disable optimistic concurrency in client builds, 4) escalate to Eng oncall and assigned Edge owner. Keep customer comms channel warm and post interim status every 15 minutes.
